title: Canonical affine single-complex pushforward comparison is invertible
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be affine and $M$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-direct-image]. The map $(f_*M)[0]\to Rf_*(M[0])$ obtained by the inverse termwise single-complex comparison followed by the right-derived unit is an isomorphism in the chosen derived category. This is the specified unit composite, not an arbitrary isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 01XC, with the right-derived-unit naturality argument for an acyclic module

proof.text: Module direct image is a right adjoint, hence left exact. Affine higher-direct-image vanishing makes M right-acyclic. Zero terms are right-acyclic as well, so every term of M[0] is.
Choose a bounded-below resolution i:M[0]->I with injective terms. Injective objects are right-acyclic, and bounded-below injective complexes are K-injective.
Apply quasiIso_map_of_rightAcyclic to i. Thus Q(F(i)) is invertible, as is RF(Q(i)). The unit is invertible at the K-injective complex I.

Naturality gives Q(F(i)) >> unit(I) = unit(M[0]) >> RF(Q(i)). Cancel the invertible last factor to obtain an invertible unit at M[0]. Compose with Q of the single-complex isomorphism. This is exactly the morphism in the statement.
